openTomorrow: Yeah, absolutely. I'd open it first thing to log my gym session and snap my photo. This Strict mode doesn't mess around - you miss a day, you start over. That's the whole point for me.
secured: I'm guessing it means my progress is locked in or verified somehow - like the app confirms I actually did what I said I did, maybe through the photos or some validation system so I can't cheat.
freeze: That's probably a pause button for the challenge. Life happens - if I get injured or have an emergency, I can freeze my progress instead of losing everything. But I'm not planning to use it.
selfReported: That's when I manually log stuff myself instead of the app tracking it automatically. I'm taking photos every day anyway, so it's documented, but I'm still the one reporting it happened.
best: Seeing that 'Gym before works' habit staring at me on the screen. It's real. It's committed. Picking Strict mode felt like drawing a line - this is exactly the accountability I need.
worst: The character limit thing with only 60 characters. I wanted to write more detail about my goals but got cut off. Felt restrictive, ironic for a challenge app.
tellFriend: 100%. I'd tell my buddy Marcus - oh wait, that's me - I'd tell my crew: 'Download GRIIT, pick Strict, and actually commit. Photo proof every day, no wiggle room. If you're serious about changing your habits, this forces you to be serious.'
